_help: Each run (once a day, evening Toronto) publishes the oldest due post, on or after its 'date' (YYYY-MM-DD, Toronto time); one post per date means one post per day. 'video' is an MP4 in social/videos/ (Instagram Reel + LinkedIn video; not Facebook), 'image' a JPEG in social/images/. 'platforms': any of facebook, instagram, story (Instagram Story), linkedin. Optional 'instagram' / 'linkedin' objects ({caption, hashtags, title}) override the shared text on that platform. Published ids are recorded in social/posted.json.

For some kids, it never logs off. 📱💔

Bullying follows kids home: into group chats, DMs and late-night messages. It's not “just kids being kids.”

👀 Watch for:
• Afraid to go to school
• “Sick” every morning
• Grades dropping
• Suddenly secretive online

✅ What to do:
1️⃣ Listen. Don't blame.
2️⃣ Save the messages.
3️⃣ Report it to the school, in writing.
4️⃣ No action? Go to the school board.
5️⃣ Threats? Call the police.

Kids, you're not alone 💜 Kids Help Phone: call 1-800-668-6868 or text CONNECT to 686868. Free, 24/7.

linkedin.title: For some kids, it never logs off: spotting and stopping bullying
linkedin.caption:
Bullying doesn't end when the school bell rings. For many kids, it follows them home on their phones.

A short checklist for parents, teachers and coaches:

Warning signs
• Fear of going to school, or skipping it
• Feeling “sick” before school
• A drop in grades
• Avoiding devices, or becoming secretive online

What to do
1. Listen first. Don't blame the child.
2. Save the messages as evidence.
3. Report it to the teacher and principal in writing, and ask what the school's bullying prevention policy requires.
4. If the school doesn't act, take it to the school board.
5. If there are threats, report it to the police.

Kids and teens can reach Kids Help Phone 24/7, free: call 1-800-668-6868 or text CONNECT to 686868.

ComplaintCA helps families in Canada find the right place to file a school complaint, free and with an anonymous option: https://www.complaintca.ca
